In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $x(2x-1),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit. 

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $x,$ and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $2x-1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{2x-1}-\frac{3}{x} & = \\ \frac{x}{x}\cdot \frac{6}{2x-1}-\frac{2x-1}{2x-1}\cdot \frac{3}{x} & = \\ \frac{6x}{x(2x-1)}-\frac{3(2x-1)}{x(2x-1)} & = \\ \frac{6x-3(2x-1)}{x(2x-1)} & = \\ \frac{6x-6x+3}{x(2x-1)} & = \\ \frac{3}{x(2x-1)}\end{aligned}
$$
